section: Claude models overview > Reading notes
text:
## Reading notes

The overview consolidates active model capabilities, context windows, output limits, speed and links to pricing. These are dynamic fields. Build a shortlist from the official page, then evaluate candidates on the organization's own task set.

section: Claude models overview > Enterprise selection questions
text:
## Enterprise selection questions

- Is the workload reasoning-, speed- or cost-sensitive
- Are context and output limits sufficient
- Are tool use and vision required
- How will model updates affect reproducibility?

section: Claude API pricing and prompt caching > Reading notes

section: Claude API pricing and prompt caching > Enterprise selection questions
text:

- How much input is repeated
- Can cache hits offset cache-write costs
- What invalidates cache breakpoints
- Does the estimate include input, output, cache and tool costs?

text:

The list covers prompt injection, insecure output handling, training-data poisoning, denial of service, supply-chain vulnerabilities, sensitive information disclosure, insecure plugin design, excessive agency, overreliance and model theft. section: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 > Enterprise selection questions

section: Enterprise LLM Selection Checklist
text: # Enterprise LLM Selection Checklist

section: Enterprise LLM Selection Checklist > A. Business requirements
text:
## A. Business requirements

- [ ] Define tasks: support, knowledge Q&A, coding, document processing, agents, vision, etc.
- [ ] Prepare a representative, de-identified evaluation set.
- [ ] Define quality metrics: accuracy, factuality, task success, refusal quality and tool-call success.
- [ ] Define service metrics: P50/P95/P99 latency, throughput, concurrency and availability.
- [ ] Estimate the cost of wrong answers, wrong tool calls and human rework.

section: Enterprise LLM Selection Checklist > B. Model capability
text:
## B. Model capability

- [ ] Chinese/English and domain terminology.
- [ ] Reasoning, coding, long documents and multi-turn context.
- [ ] Vision/audio/video requirements.
- [ ] Function calling, tool use and structured output.
- [ ] Context window and maximum output.
- [ ] Refusal, safety and adversarial robustness.
- [ ] Results on the organization's own evaluation set.

section: Enterprise LLM Selection Checklist > C. Deployment and infrastructure
text:
## C. Deployment and infrastructure

- [ ] API hosting, dedicated deployment or fully private hosting.
- [ ] Region, data residency and network access.
- [ ] GPU type, VRAM, interconnect and compute budget.
- [ ] vLLM/SGLang/Transformers compatibility.
- [ ] Quantization quality regression.
- [ ] Parallelism, scaling, rollout and rollback.

section: Enterprise LLM Selection Checklist > D. Total cost of ownership
text:
## D. Total cost of ownership

- [ ] Input/output tokens and cache-hit assumptions.
- [ ] Peak/off-peak prices, rate limits and minimum spend.
- [ ] GPU, storage, network and operations costs.
- [ ] Cost per successful task, not just price per million tokens.
- [ ] Retries, agent turns and tool costs.
- [ ] Budget limits and abnormal-usage alerts.

section: Enterprise LLM Selection Checklist > E. Security, privacy and compliance
text:
## E. Security, privacy and compliance

- [ ] Whether data is used for model training and opt-out options.
- [ ] Retention, deletion and ZDR scope.
- [ ] DPA, confidentiality terms, audit rights and subprocessors.
- [ ] Authentication, RBAC, MFA, key rotation and audit logs.
- [ ] Private networking, TLS and data residency.
- [ ] Prompt injection, sensitive-data disclosure and tool privilege controls.
- [ ] Model license and supply-chain review.

section: Enterprise LLM Selection Checklist > F. Vendor and operations
text:
## F. Vendor and operations

- [ ] SLA, support response, status and incident notification.
- [ ] Model upgrades, deprecation and compatibility policy.
- [ ] Price-change notices and contract protection.
- [ ] Vendor lock-in and migration strategy.
- [ ] Monitoring for quality, latency, tokens, cost and errors.
- [ ] Regular re-evaluation and model-change approval.

section: Enterprise LLM Selection Checklist > Suggested scoring weights (adjust to the use case)
text:
## Suggested scoring weights (adjust to the use case)

| Dimension | Weight |
|---|---:|
| Business task quality | 30% |
| Security, privacy and compliance | 20% |
| Deployment feasibility and reliability | 15% |
| Total cost of ownership | 15% |
| Latency, throughput and scalability | 10% |
| Vendor support and portability | 10% |

Do not select a model only by public benchmarks or parameter count. Compare at least 2-3 candidates on the same evaluation set, prompt, decoding configuration and load conditions.

section: Enterprise Requirements (Synthetic Internal)
text:
# Enterprise Requirements (Synthetic Internal)

> **Source status:** This is a self-constructed example for enterprise model-selection research. It is not a real company's internal policy, requirement, procurement record, or approved standard.

section: Enterprise Requirements (Synthetic Internal) > Metadata
text:
## Metadata

```json
{
  "source_type": "synthetic_internal",
  "document_name": "enterprise_requirements.md"
}
```

section: Enterprise Requirements (Synthetic Internal) > Purpose
text:
## Purpose

This document provides a sample set of enterprise requirements for structuring a large-language-model selection exercise. It is intended for demonstration, comparison, and evaluation planning only.

section: Enterprise Requirements (Synthetic Internal) > 1. Business and task requirements
text:
## 1. Business and task requirements

- Identify target business scenarios before selecting a model.
- Prepare a representative, de-identified evaluation set for each scenario.
- Define task-quality metrics such as accuracy, factual consistency, task completion rate, tool-call success rate, and refusal quality.
- Define service objectives, including P50/P95/P99 latency, throughput, concurrency, and availability.
- Record the impact and handling cost of incorrect outputs.

section: Enterprise Requirements (Synthetic Internal) > 2. Model capability requirements
text:
## 2. Model capability requirements

- Evaluate Chinese and English performance and domain terminology.
- Evaluate reasoning, code generation, long-document processing, and multi-turn dialogue where relevant.
- Confirm whether vision, audio, or video input is required.
- Test function calling, tool use, and structured output against actual application schemas.
- Verify context-window and maximum-output limits.
- Evaluate robustness to prompt injection and unsafe requests.

section: Enterprise Requirements (Synthetic Internal) > 3. Deployment and infrastructure requirements
text:
## 3. Deployment and infrastructure requirements

- Compare hosted API, dedicated deployment, and fully self-hosted deployment.
- Confirm data residency, region availability, and network-access requirements.
- Estimate GPU memory and compute needs, including model weights and KV cache.
- Test compatibility with the intended serving stack, such as vLLM.
- Benchmark quantized and unquantized configurations on target hardware.
- Define scaling, rollout, rollback, health-check, and capacity-test procedures.

section: Enterprise Requirements (Synthetic Internal) > 4. Cost requirements
text:
## 4. Cost requirements

- Estimate input, output, and cached-token usage from representative traffic.
- Include API charges, dedicated capacity, GPU rental or depreciation, storage, networking, and operations.
- Calculate cost per successful task, not only price per million tokens.
- Include retries, multi-step agent calls, and tool execution overhead.
- Define budget limits, quotas, and abnormal-usage alerts.

section: Enterprise Requirements (Synthetic Internal) > 5. Security, privacy, and compliance requirements
text:
## 5. Security, privacy, and compliance requirements

- Verify whether prompts and outputs may be used for provider model training.
- Review data-retention periods, deletion processes, and any Zero Data Retention eligibility and exceptions.
- Review data-processing agreements, confidentiality terms, subprocessors, and audit rights.
- Require authentication, least-privilege access, secret rotation, and audit logging.
- Review private networking, encryption, and data-residency controls.
- Assess prompt injection, sensitive-data leakage, unsafe output handling, and excessive agent permissions.
- Record model licenses and third-party software or model-supply-chain risks.

section: Enterprise Requirements (Synthetic Internal) > 6. Vendor and operational requirements
text:
## 6. Vendor and operational requirements

- Review SLA, support response times, incident communication, and service-status reporting.
- Understand model-version changes, deprecation periods, and compatibility guarantees.
- Review pricing-change notice and contractual price protections.
- Assess vendor lock-in and define a model migration or multi-provider fallback plan.
- Monitor quality, latency, token usage, cost, errors, and user feedback.
- Require periodic re-evaluation after model, prompt, data, or deployment changes.

section: Enterprise Requirements (Synthetic Internal) > 7. Suggested evaluation weights
text:
## 7. Suggested evaluation weights

These weights are illustrative and should be adjusted to the actual business context.

| Evaluation dimension                   | Suggested weight |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------: |
| Business-task quality                  |              30% |
| Security, privacy, and compliance      |              20% |
| Deployment feasibility and reliability |              15% |
| Total cost of ownership                |              15% |
| Latency, throughput, and scalability   |              10% |
| Vendor support and portability         |              10% |

section: Enterprise Requirements (Synthetic Internal) > 8. Evaluation procedure
text:
## 8. Evaluation procedure

1. Shortlist at least two or three candidate models.
2. Use the same de-identified task set, prompts, decoding settings, and evaluation rules.
3. Record model identifiers, version/date, endpoint or deployment configuration, hardware, and serving framework.
4. Measure task quality, latency, throughput, token usage, and cost.
5. Run security and privacy reviews separately from capability tests.
6. Document trade-offs, unresolved risks, and the reason for the final selection.

section: Enterprise Requirements (Synthetic Internal) > Important limitation
text:
## Important limitation

This document is synthetic and illustrative. It must not be represented as an actual enterprise's internal requirements, policy, compliance approval, procurement specification, or evidence of production use. Replace or validate every requirement with the relevant organization's approved materials before making real procurement or deployment decisions.
